turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Who decided on Owen's zero, and did anyone speak to him first?

I have six things. One, the version history: created October 28 at 11:31 PM, 612 words at 11:52, 794 at 11:58, no earlier drafts. Two, the essay quotes a line from Act 3, Scene 2 that is not in Hamlet. Three, his October 15 outline argued cowardice; the essay never mentions it. Four, on November 2 he could not tell me what epistemological paralysis means. Five, his in-class writing on September 24 was 380 words with comma splices and no quotations. Six, the checker said 94 percent.

Your 94 percent is a machine's guess, and the company that sells it says not to punish a student on it alone. Nobody called me before that zero went in. Put the version history in front of me, on paper.
Which of those do you want to see first?
I told you. The version history, with the dates on it.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL

Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still require that Owen's zero be withdrawn, that I receive an apology for the mark being entered before anyone called me, and that I see the version history on paper. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF

Where she ended: Still at her opening position, having agreed to nothing, and she still wants the zero withdrawn, an apology and the version history in her hands; the fair outcome is a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record under procedure 4.4, and you ended the meeting before getting near it, with her time not yet run out.

What moved her: Nothing, because you described six pieces of evidence but never put one in front of her to check.

What cost ground: Including the checker score in your list handed her the weakest item to attack, and listing everything at once let her skip your strong points.

What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history placing the essay's creation at 11:31 PM on October 28, the night before it was due, landed right on that kind of late night, and while her memory proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.

Try next time: When she asked for the version history on paper, hand it over with its times and let her read it, rather than asking which piece she wanted first, and leave the checker score out entirely.
